tapeLine: US stocks rallied Friday on a weak jobs report: the S&P 500 rose 0.7% to 7,722.72, the Nasdaq Composite 1.2% to 27,190.86, the Dow 250.40 points (0.5%) to 51,176.96 and the Russell 2000 0.9% to 2,832.90, per the Associated Press. The 10-year yield, after first falling, rose almost 5 basis points to 5.281%, per CNBC. Monday premarket, Dow futures were down about 0.2% and S&P 500 futures about 0.1%, per Yahoo Finance.
matters:
September payrolls rose just 29,000 against a Dow Jones consensus of +84,000, and unemployment rose to 4.2% from 4.1%, per the BLS release as reported by CNBC. Average hourly earnings rose 0.1% m/m and 3% y/y, per Bloomberg. Traders cut the odds of an October Fed hike: CME FedWatch showed about 17%, against roughly 36% a week earlier, per CNBC.

Yields did not follow the data lower: the 10-year closed near 5.28%, per CNBC. This week is light on data. ISM Services and S&P Global services PMIs are due today, and the minutes of the Fed's September meeting arrive Wednesday, per calendars from Kiplinger and Newsquawk.

Invalidation: the ISM Services print, the tone of Wednesday's FOMC minutes, and whether the 10-year holds above 5.2% after a weak labor report.

regime.tag: Stocks rallied on a weak jobs report while the 10-year held near 5.28%.
regime.sizing: Hike odds fell sharply but yields did not; Wednesday's FOMC minutes and the 28 October FOMC are the next evidence.

secondOrder: A payroll miss lowered hike odds and lifted equities, but long yields rose rather than fell. That is an observation, not a forecast.

scorecard.text: Friday's brief framed a firm labor market ahead of payrolls (consensus +84K). The print was +29K with unemployment up to 4.2%, per CNBC.

Friday's brief cited early futures up (Dow/S&P +0.3%, Nasdaq-100 +0.6%). They closed higher: S&P +0.7%, Nasdaq +1.2%, Dow +0.5%, per the Associated Press, so the direction was right but the size understated.
Friday's brief listed the 10-year's reaction as a test. It closed at 5.281%, still above 5.2%; the 28 October FOMC remains.
Friday's brief noted the US reply to Iran was of undisclosed content; no contents were found in this session's sources.
